clue.text: Down under, one runs wild, pocketing litter

definitions.text: Down under, one runs wild, pocketing litter

parts.words: Down under, one runs wild, pocketing litter
parts.note: read as an Australian creature living in the wild that carries its young in a pouch, while the surface suggests a vandal stuffing rubbish into their pockets

explanation.surface: Someone in Australia running amok and stuffing rubbish into their pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of young, carried in the pouch of this marsupial from the island state south of mainland Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a wild carnivorous marsupial found only on an Australian island, and like all marsupials its young ride in a pouch.

clue.text: Dramatic affairs of Sicilians interest the law, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these three words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Sicilian goings-on attract the attention of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns INTEREST THE LAW into the title of Shakespeare's play, much of which is set at the court of Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance opens at the court of King Leontes of Sicilia, so it is a drama about Sicilian goings-on.

clue.text: Potters bar, say

parts.note: read as an obstacle met by those potting balls on a green baize table, while the surface names the Hertfordshire town Potters Bar

explanation.surface: Potters Bar given as an example of a commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar is a town just north of London. Here 'potters' are cue-sport players who pot balls, and a position that bars their shot gives this game its name.
explanation.definitionFit: In this cue game a player is blocked from hitting the target ball directly, a position named after the game itself; its players pot balls.

clue.text: Indian mufti changed endlessly

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Muslim legal scholar from India keeps changing his mind without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the eleven letters of INDIAN MUFTI into the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'to infinity', used for something going on without limit.

clue.text: Going out at nine for constitutional

indicators.note: going out in the sense of being disordered tells us the letters of the two following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Heading out for a walk at nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitutional' looks like a noun for a healthy walk, which the surface supports, but it is the adjective meaning part of one's makeup; 'Going out' rearranges AT NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constitutional belongs to a person's basic nature, inborn rather than learnt.

clue.text: Vikings, or riders with new leader

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the riders word, which is swapped for the letter from new

parts.note: riders on horseback are horsemen

explanation.surface: A choice between Vikings and cavalry under a new commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new leader' means HORSEMEN gets a fresh first letter: its H gives way to N.
explanation.definitionFit: The seafaring Scandinavian raiders of the early Middle Ages are also called men of the north.

clue.text: One does not fly with English musicians

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union, the British trade union for performers

explanation.surface: Someone who avoids air travel, going with a group of English players.
explanation.walkthrough: The MU is the Musicians' Union, the UK trade union for working musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Australian bird is flightless, so it is one creature that never takes to the air.

clue.text: Formality over issue, say, of cold sheet at sea

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: icy reserve or stiffness of manner is often called ice, as in breaking the ice

indicators.note: say tells us the word for issue is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an issue is an outflow or stream, a flow

explanation.surface: Deciding a point of etiquette over the issue of a chilly bedsheet on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks FLOW (issue) as heard, spelt FLOE. 'over' places ICE above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating flat expanse of frozen seawater is a sheet of ice drifting in the ocean.

clue.text: Strangely, he endures a wife for so long in Germany

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the four following words appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A man oddly puts up with his wife for a lengthy stay in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges HE ENDURES A WIFE. 'so long' looks like a stretch of time but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase for goodbye literally means 'until we see again', like the casual farewell 'so long'.

clue.text: Elgar's first movement, with feeling

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: motion means movement

explanation.surface: The opening movement of an Elgar work played expressively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical, given Elgar, but here it is just motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling such as love or anger is a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Said to regret low pile of coins

indicators.note: said marks the following words as spoken, to be matched to a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to regret is to rue, and low means low, so the phrase gives rue low

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to feel bad about a small stack of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' tells us to say RUE LOW aloud to get the French-derived word for a wrapped roll of coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a cylindrical stack of coins wrapped in paper, as issued by banks.

clue.text: Character of the Italian king

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The personality of an Italian monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: IL is 'the' in Italian; K is king, as in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a kind or sort, as in 'people of that type', the character of a group.

clue.text: Pop of the Dutch, say?

parts.note: read with dutch as old slang for wife, so pop of the dutch is the dad of one's spouse

explanation.surface: A Dutch father, or a fizzy drink from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' (or 'old dutch') is old cockney slang for a wife, so her pop is your spouse's father.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's wife's father becomes his relative by marriage, a family member gained through a wedding.

clue.text: Rash, from placing one fur under broken divan

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the fur below the broken piece

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the furniture word are jumbled

parts.note: sable is a costly fur from a weasel-like animal

explanation.surface: A reckless act: putting a fur coat under a broken couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning unwise. 'broken' jumbles the couch to NADVI; 'under' sets the fur beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash course of action is unwise or ill-judged, a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Bishop's seat overturned, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the word for overturned is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: something overturned has been thrown down

explanation.surface: A bishop's chair has been knocked over, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells us THROWN (overturned) is heard, giving a word for a bishop's chair of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's official chair in his cathedral is his ceremonial seat, a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: People in high places born to hold stakes

indicators.note: to hold says the birth word contains the stakes word within it

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name
pales are pointed wooden stakes, as in a fence

explanation.surface: Those in positions of power were born to keep a share of the wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People in high places' suggests the elite, but means the inhabitants of a Himalayan country. 'to hold' puts the stakes inside the birth word.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of a Himalayan kingdom live among the world's highest mountains.

clue.text: In bakery, the machinery produces redness of skin

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Equipment in a bakery causes skin irritation in the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside bakERY THE MAchinery.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names superficial reddening of the skin caused by dilated blood vessels.

clue.text: Songbird giving cardinal a fright?

parts.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, from the robes of cardinals
a start is a sudden jump or fright

explanation.surface: A bird startling a church cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' seems to be a person, or even the red bird, but it is the colour red.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Eurasian bird of the thrush family is known for its fiery orange tail.

clue.text: Lose hope in Slough?

definitions.meaning: to lose hope is to give up all expectation, the verb sense
a slough is a bog, and figuratively a state of deep dejection, as in Bunyan's Slough of Despond

explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also a town west of London, made famous as a dreary place; here it is the bog of hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are hopelessness: the verb for giving up all expectation, and the noun for a mire of dejection.

clue.text: Reluctant to write a poem

parts.note: a short poem or stanza is verse

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to compose a piece of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disinclined or opposed to something is a synonym for unwilling.

clue.text: Has life inside kingdom, taking the practical view

indicators.note: inside says the existence word sits within the kingdom word

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom
to have life is simply to exist, so the phrase gives is

explanation.surface: Someone thriving in a monarchy and seeing things as they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has life' means exists, as in 'he lives' becoming 'he is'; 'inside' sets that within the kingdom word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the attitude of accepting things as they actually are, being pragmatic rather than idealistic.

clue.text: Reticent about one right cross

indicators.note: about tells us the shy word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a shy person is reticent
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A reserved person is upset about one particular entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the reticent word round one and right. 'cross' could be a crucifix or a verb, but it is the adjective meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British informal for bad-tempered or annoyed, as in getting irritable.

clue.text: Trial marriages played out in st John's wood

definitions.text: played out in st John's wood

parts.note: a test is a trial
a good marriage is often called a match

explanation.surface: Trial marriages being acted out in a London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: St John's Wood is the London district home to Lord's, the famous cricket ground where international five-day games are played.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's cricket ground in St John's Wood hosts the international five-day games of cricket.

clue.text: Variety of sad notices

indicators.note: a variety of the word sad is another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An assortment of gloomy announcements.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for advertisements, which are public notices put up to sell or announce.

clue.text: Left bunch of keys in foliage

parts.note: musical keys are named by the letters A to G, so a bunch of them can be any string of those letters, here E A F A G E

explanation.surface: A forgotten set of keys among the leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' are not door keys but musical keys, named A to G; the six needed here, E, A, F, A, G, E, all fall in that range.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a collective term for leaves, the greenery of plants.

clue.text: Friend in France in the morning, at one

parts.note: am stands for ante meridiem, before noon
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Meeting a French friend in the morning at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at one' seems a time of day; here 'at' is a link and 'one' is the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a male friend or pal.

clue.text: Litter spread twice in front of hospital

indicators.note: in front of places the first pieces before the hospital letter

parts.note: to rub ointment on is to spread it
bis is a Latin word for twice, used in music for a repeat
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Rubbish was strewn twice before the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS, Latin for 'twice', is written on scores to mean repeat a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is discarded waste or refuse scattered about.

clue.text: But it is not necessarily plain sailing for him!

definitions.text: But it is not necessarily plain sailing for him!

parts.words: But it is not necessarily plain sailing for him!
parts.note: read with plain as ordinary and sailing as seafaring, so a common sailor of the lowest rank whose life is far from easy

explanation.surface: Life is not always easy for a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' points to the word meaning common or usual, and 'sailing' to a man at sea; the joke is that his job is anything but easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank is the lowest grade of sailor in the Royal Navy, an unskilled hand on deck.
